name: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report
why: The WPSR is the anchor public inventory release for WTI, especially crude, gasoline, distillates and refinery utilization.

name: EIA Today in Energy RSS
why: Timely official energy-market analysis is useful context for inventories, demand and infrastructure trends.

name: EIA press releases RSS
why: Captures official announcements, outlook changes and methodology notes that can reset market expectations.

name: EIA gasoline and diesel RSS
why: Downstream pricing and crack-spread context help the swarm reason about refinery demand and product tightness.

name: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook
why: The STEO provides official demand, supply and price outlook revisions that shape the medium-term oil narrative.

name: EIA API documentation
why: Best source for structured inventory, production and refinery data once you add series-specific adapters.

name: EIA open data browser
why: Helpful for discovering the exact series you want to bind into the oil context pipeline.
notes: Treat this as a discovery source, not a direct headline feed.

name: CFTC Commitments of Traders
why: Positioning helps detect crowded oil trades and whether inventory reactions may extend or mean revert.

name: NOAA National Hurricane Center tropical weather outlook RSS
why: Storm threats can materially affect Gulf production, refining and shipping infrastructure.

name: NOAA NHC Atlantic outlook RSS
why: Adds Atlantic storm bulletins and updates that often matter for oil more than broad macro headlines do.

name: OPEC Monthly Oil Market Report
why: OPEC demand, supply and balance revisions shape the global oil narrative and can move front-month crude.
notes: Valuable but not ideal for the auto-fetch path because the site and downloadable artifacts are less scrape-friendly.

name: IEA Oil Market Report
why: A high-signal global oil balance source, especially for demand revisions and inventory interpretation.
notes: Paid and delayed; include manually if you have access, otherwise use public release metadata only.

name: MINING.com oil sands RSS
why: Useful for Canada-heavy supply and infrastructure headlines that can bleed into North American crude narratives.
